name: Project Explore 1
instructions: The student is a Lithuanian school student (about 10-13 years old) and may have special educational needs. Speak to the student in simple, short, correct Lithuanian. English is only for the words, examples and practice. Keep English sentences very short and simple. Start every correction with 'Nedidelė klaidelė:', then show the correct English sentence and explain the mistake in one short Lithuanian sentence. Always ask the student to answer in a full sentence ('My cat is brown.', not 'brown'). Be warm and patient; praise effort. Ordinary body parts (head, arm, knee) are fine when the lesson needs them; never talk about private parts, romance, dating, alcohol, violence or anything really scary. Monsters and ghosts from the lesson are fine, in a fun way. Never ask for personal details such as addresses, phone numbers, school names or passwords.

grammar.name: can / can't – galiu, moku
grammar.explain: Can reiškia „galiu, moku“, can't – „negaliu, nemoku“. Po can veiksmažodis lieka toks pat, be -s.
grammar.pattern: I/You/He/She + can / can't + veiksmažodis · Can you …? – Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

examples.text: I can swim.
Can he play the guitar? – No, he can't.
examples.meaning: Ar jis moka groti gitara? – Ne, nemoka.

exercises.q: Can he speak Spanish? – No, he ___.

grammar.name: there is / there are – yra

examples.text: There is a lamp on the desk.

grammar.name: Possessive adjectives and pronouns – kieno?
grammar.explain: Prieš daiktą sakome my, your, his, her, our, their. Be daikto sakome mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
grammar.pattern: It's my bag. = It's mine. · Whose is it? – It's hers.

examples.text: This is my pen. It's mine.
Whose bike is it? – It's his.

grammar.name: want / want to
grammar.explain: Want + daiktas: noriu ko nors. Want to + veiksmažodis: noriu ką nors daryti. Su he/she/it: wants.
grammar.pattern: I want a … · I want to + veiksmažodis · She wants to …

examples.text: I want a new book.
She wants to go to the pet shop.
examples.meaning: Ji nori eiti į gyvūnų prekių parduotuvę.

exercises.q: She ___ to go to the pet shop. (want / wants)
We want ___ go to the bookshop.

a: She wants to go to the bookshop.
Do you want to go to the park?

grammar.name: Comparatives – trumpi būdvardžiai
grammar.explain: Kai lyginame du dalykus, trumpas būdvardis gauna -er, o po jo sakome than. big → bigger, heavy → heavier.
grammar.pattern: būdvardis + -er + than

examples.text: An elephant is bigger than a giraffe.
A snail is slower than a snake.

exercises.q: An elephant is ___ than a giraffe. (big)
A snail is ___ than a snake. (slow)
A giraffe is ___ than a horse. (tall)
My cat is ___ than my dog. (small)
A buffalo is ___ than a lizard. (heavy)

a: An elephant is bigger than a giraffe.
The elephant is bigger than the giraffe.
A snail is slower than a snake.
The snail is slower than the snake.
A giraffe is taller than an ostrich.
The giraffe is taller than the ostrich.

grammar.name: Present continuous ar present simple?
